# nxos_epbr (Resource)

This resource can manage the Enhanced Policy-Based Redirect (ePBR) configuration on NX-OS devices, including services with layer-3, layer-2 and DPU endpoints, reverse endpoints and probes, service chains, failover groups, policies with matches and sequences, VRF redirection, infra VLANs and interface policy attachments.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_epbr" "example" {
  services = {
    "SVC1" = {
      admin_state                    = "shut"
      connection_mode                = "full-duplex"
      hold_down_threshold_count      = 3
      hold_down_threshold_time       = 100
      reverse_security_group         = 200
      security_group                 = 100
      service_interface              = "eth1/10"
      threshold_up                   = 50
      type                           = "l3"
      vrf                            = "default"
      probe_control                  = "enable"
      probe_frequency                = 5
      probe_port                     = 80
      probe_protocol                 = "TCP"
      probe_retry_down_count         = 2
      probe_retry_up_count           = 2
      probe_reverse_source_interface = "lo123"
      probe_source_interface         = "lo123"
      probe_timeout                  = 3
      endpoints = {
        "10.1.1.10" = {
          admin_state               = "shut"
          hold_down_threshold_count = 3
          hold_down_threshold_time  = 100
          mode                      = "hot-standby"
          weight                    = 3
          probe_frequency           = 60
          probe_http_get            = "index.html"
          probe_http_version        = "1.1"
          probe_protocol            = "HTTP"
          probe_retry_down_count    = 2
          probe_retry_up_count      = 2
          probe_source_interface    = "lo123"
          probe_timeout             = 30
          reverse_ip                = "10.2.2.10"
          reverse_probe_protocol    = "noProtocol"
          reverse_probe_track_id    = 10
        }
      }
    }
  }
  failover_groups = {
    "FG1" = {
      service_chains = {
        "CHAIN2" = {
          preference = 10
        }
      }
    }
  }
  service_chains = {
    "CHAIN1" = {
      failover_group      = "FG1"
      load_balance_method = "src"
      mode                = "multisite"
      sequences = {
        "10" = {
          service             = "SVC2"
          action              = "route"
          load_balance_method = "dst"
          reverse_action      = "route"
        }
      }
    }
  }
  policies = {
    "POL1" = {
      default_traffic_action = "redirect"
      destination_vrf        = "default"
      source_vrf             = "default"
      statistics             = true
      matches = {
        "EPBR-ACL1" = {
          access_list_type    = "ipv4"
          buckets             = 8
          destination_vrf     = "default"
          load_balance_method = "src"
          mask_position       = 2
          source_vrf          = "default"
          traffic_action      = "redirect"
          sequences = {
            "10" = {
              service     = "SVC3"
              fail_action = "drop"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  infra_vlans = {
    "100" = {}
  }
  interfaces = {
    "eth1/11;ipv4;no-reverse" = {
      policy = "POL1"
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `failover_groups` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR failover groups.
  - Map key: `name` - The name of the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--failover_groups))
- `infra_vlans` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR infra VLANs.
  - Map key: `vlans` - Infra VLAN range. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--infra_vlans))
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR interface policy attachments.
  - Map key format: `<interface_id>;<ip_type>;<reverse>`
  - Key component `interface_id`: Interface ID.
  - Key component `ip_type`: IP type. Choices: `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `l2`.
  - Key component `reverse`: Reverse policy. Choices: `no-reverse`, `reverse`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))
- `policies` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR policies.
  - Map key: `name` - The name of the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies))
- `service_chains` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR service chains.
  - Map key: `name` - The name of the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_chains))
- `services` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR services.
  - Map key: `name` - The name of the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))
- `vrfs` (Attributes Map) List of ePBR VRF redirection policies.
  - Map key: `name` - The name of the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vrfs))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_epbr.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_epbr for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_epbr.example ""
```
